tasks.prompt: Order the response when a trickling filter distributor arm stops rotating.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: distributor found stationary during a routine round.

cards.label: Look for blocked nozzles or debris jamming the arm
Check whether flow is still reaching the filter
Log the stoppage, the cause, and the run time lost
Restore feed and confirm the arm rotates freely
Clear the nozzles and remove the obstruction
Stop the feed to the filter and apply lockout if the arm must be freed by hand

tasks.explanation: Flow and blockage checks come first, lockout protects any hands on work, and rotation is proven again before the event is logged.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for raising recirculation on a trickling filter during dry weather low flow.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: influent flow low, media surface beginning to dry between doses.

cards.label: Measure or read the current recirculation rate
Check the current influent flow to the filter
Record the new recirculation ratio in the log
Check that the media surface stays wetted between doses
Confirm the distributor still rotates at the higher rate
Increase the recirculation pump output or valve opening in one step

tasks.explanation: Current rates are known before adjustment, distributor performance is confirmed at the new rate, and media wetting is the acceptance check.

tasks.prompt: Order the response to ponding on the surface of a trickling filter.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: wastewater ponding on the media surface instead of filtering through.

cards.label: Check distributor flow and nozzle condition over the ponded area
Inspect the ponded area and check for heavy slime growth
Log the ponding location, cause, and corrective action
Return the filter to service gradually and watch for ponding returning
Flush the surface at a high rate or rest the filter as directed by the supervisor
Reduce the hydraulic load to the filter by shifting flow to the other filter

tasks.explanation: Inspection identifies the cause area before load is cut, flushing or resting follows the load reduction, and return to service is gradual.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for starting a rotating biological contactor unit.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: RBC shaft and media in an empty tank, drive unit serviced.

cards.label: Remove lockout devices and restore power to the drive
Inspect the shaft, media discs, and drive and remove all debris
Check the forming slime layer and effluent quality over the first days
Begin influent feed at a low rate
Start the drive and confirm slow, even rotation
Fill the tank with primary effluent to the normal shaft immersion level

tasks.explanation: The unit is inspected dry, power returns before filling so rotation can start as soon as the level is right, and feed ramps up as biomass forms.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for shutting down an RBC unit for internal inspection.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: one RBC train, other trains remain in service.

cards.label: Stop the influent feed to the unit
Divert influent feed to the remaining RBC trains
Ventilate and test the atmosphere before any entry and post the inspection notice
Apply lockout to the drive and feed equipment
Stop the drive once the tank is drained
Drain the tank contents back to the plant inlet

tasks.explanation: Feed diversion and draining come before the drive stops, lockout follows, and atmospheric testing is the last gate before entry.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for dealing with excessive biomass growth on an RBC.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: drive motor amps climbing, thick grey growth visible on the media.

cards.label: Inspect the media for growth thickness and odour
Record the drive motor amps and compare them with the normal range
Log the amps, settings changed, and effluent observations
Recheck motor amps after the sloughing period
Watch effluent solids as the excess biomass sloughs off
Adjust submergence or air drive settings as the manufacturer directs to encourage sloughing

tasks.explanation: Amps quantify the problem before adjustment, sloughing is induced by the manufacturer method, and amps are rechecked to prove the correction.

tasks.prompt: Order the winter operating checks for an outdoor trickling filter.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: freezing temperatures, distributor and nozzles at risk of icing.

cards.label: Clear ice safely from walkways before working near the filter
Inspect the distributor arms and end nozzles for ice build up
Log temperatures, ice conditions, and actions taken
Monitor the filter effluent for signs of short circuiting
Check that all nozzles are passing flow and none are frozen shut
Increase recirculation to keep wastewater moving through the filter

tasks.explanation: Ice is identified and walkways made safe first, recirculation keeps water moving, nozzle checks confirm even distribution, and conditions are logged.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for starting a secondary clarifier.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: empty secondary clarifier, aeration basin in service and ready to feed it.

cards.label: Close the drain valve and open the return sludge line
Inspect the drive, scrapers, and baffles and remove all debris
Check effluent clarity and blanket depth as loading steadies
Start the return sludge pump at a low rate once a blanket forms
Start the collector drive as the tank fills
Open the mixed liquor inlet gate and fill the clarifier

tasks.explanation: Inspection and line up precede filling, return pumping waits for a blanket to exist, and clarity checks confirm startup at steady load.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for starting a return activated sludge pump.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: centrifugal RAS pump, suction from the secondary clarifier hopper.

cards.label: Start the pump motor
Open the discharge valve gradually to the set position
Set the pump speed or valve to the target return rate
Verify the flow meter reading and check the pump for leaks and vibration
Log the start time and the return rate
Check that the suction and discharge valves are in their correct positions
Prime the pump casing if the design requires priming

tasks.explanation: Valve line up and priming precede the start, the discharge opens gradually, the rate is set before verification, and logging is last.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for a scheduled wasting event from the activated sludge system.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: wasting from the return sludge line to the gravity thickener.

cards.label: Confirm the thickener can accept the waste volume
Review the mixed liquor solids result and the target inventory to waste
Stop the pump at the target volume and log the volume wasted
Check the waste sludge concentration at the sample port during the run
Start the waste pump and confirm flow to the thickener
Set the waste pump rate or timer for the calculated volume

tasks.explanation: Inventory math and receiving capacity come before the pump starts, concentration is checked during the run, and the target volume ends it.

tasks.prompt: Order the response to a rising sludge blanket in a secondary clarifier.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: blanket depth increasing over two consecutive checks.

cards.label: Check that the return sludge pump is running and note its rate
Verify the blanket depth at more than one point around the clarifier
Notify the supervisor if the blanket continues to rise
Remeasure the blanket after the return change takes effect
Check influent flow split for hydraulic overload on this clarifier
Increase the return rate in one step

tasks.explanation: Verification and pump status precede the rate increase, hydraulics are checked as the other likely cause, and escalation follows a failed remeasurement.

tasks.prompt: Order the response to sludge rising in clumps on a secondary clarifier surface.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: dark sludge clumps with gas bubbles rising and breaking at the surface.

cards.label: Check the blanket depth and how long sludge has sat in the clarifier
Observe and note the rising clumps and bubble activity
Log the observations and the changes made
Monitor the surface until the rising clumps stop
Adjust wasting as directed to reduce the sludge age
Increase the return sludge rate to remove the older sludge faster

tasks.explanation: The pattern is recognized as gas lift from old sludge, faster return removes it, wasting addresses the age, and monitoring confirms the surface clears.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for taking a secondary clarifier out of service.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: one of two secondary clarifiers, plant flow reduced for the work window.

cards.label: Close the inlet gate to the clarifier being removed
Shift mixed liquor flow to the clarifier staying in service
Wash down the tank and secure it for maintenance
Stop the collector drive and apply lockout
Drain the supernatant back to the aeration basin or plant inlet
Return the settled sludge inventory to the aeration basin with the return pump

tasks.explanation: Flow shifts first, the sludge inventory is recovered to the process before draining, lockout follows the drive stop, and washdown is last.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for removing scum and floating solids from a secondary clarifier.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: clarifier with a surface skimmer and a scum pit shared with the primary units.

cards.label: Run the skimmer to move surface material to the scum box
Check the scum baffle position and condition
Record the removal in the solids log
Flush the scum line clear and stop the pump
Start the scum pump and empty the pit to the solids stream
Flush the scum box contents into the scum pit with plant water

tasks.explanation: Material is gathered to the box before flushing, the pit is pumped before the line flush, and the removal is recorded at the end.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for measuring sludge blanket depth with a core sampler.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: blanket check at a secondary clarifier sample point.

cards.label: Close the sampler valve when it reaches the tank bottom zone
Lower the open core sampler slowly through the water column
Rinse the sampler clean before the next measurement point
Record the blanket depth with the location and time
Read the depth of the sludge layer in the clear tube
Raise the sampler steadily without shaking it

tasks.explanation: The sampler must reach the bottom before closing, the reading is taken from the raised core, recording follows the reading, and rinsing prepares the next point.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for shutting down and flushing a waste sludge line after wasting.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: wasting complete, waste line runs to the thickener.

cards.label: Close the discharge valve toward the thickener
Stop the waste sludge pump
Log the flush with the wasting record for the day
Close the flush water valve and leave the line valves in their standby positions
Flush the line back toward the process until the water runs clear
Open the flush water connection to the waste line

tasks.explanation: The pump stops before valves move, flushing follows isolation of the thickener, valves are left in standby, and the flush is logged with the wasting record.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for starting chlorine disinfection of secondary effluent.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: sodium hypochlorite feed to a baffled contact tank.

cards.label: Inspect the feed pump, lines, and safety equipment including the eyewash station
Confirm the contact tank is in service and effluent is flowing through it
Adjust the dose to hold the target residual and log the dose and residual
Measure the chlorine residual after the full contact time
Start the feed pump at the established dose setting
Check the hypochlorite storage tank level

tasks.explanation: Flow and safety checks precede chemical feed, the residual can only be judged after contact time, and dose adjustment follows that measurement.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for placing an ultraviolet disinfection channel in service.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: open channel UV system with two lamp banks and a level control weir.

cards.label: Confirm the downstream level control weir is operating
Inspect the channel, lamp racks, and wipers and remove any debris
Log the lamp status and hours at the time of startup
Verify lamp intensity readings are normal and no alarms are active
Energize the lamp banks and allow the lamps to warm up
Open the channel inlet gate and admit effluent flow

tasks.explanation: The channel and level control are proven before flow and power, lamps warm up before intensity is judged, and status is logged last.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for cleaning a UV lamp module.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: one lamp bank removed for sleeve cleaning, the second bank stays in service.

cards.label: Lift the module from the channel and place it on the cleaning rack
Switch the lamp bank off and apply lockout to its power supply
Remove the lockout, restore power, and verify lamp intensity
Lower the module back into the channel and reconnect it
Rinse the sleeves with clean water and inspect for damage
Wipe or soak the quartz sleeves with the approved cleaning solution

tasks.explanation: Power is locked out before lifting, cleaning and inspection happen on the rack, and intensity is verified only after the module is back in service.

tasks.prompt: Order the response when the effluent chlorine residual tests below target.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: grab sample at the contact tank outlet reads below the licence target.

cards.label: Check the feed pump operation and the hypochlorite tank level
Retest a fresh sample using the DPD method to confirm the low result
Notify the supervisor and log the event if the residual is still low
Retest the residual after another full contact time
Increase the dose in one step as the procedure allows
Check the current dose setting against the flow

tasks.explanation: Confirmation comes before equipment checks, the dose rises only after supply and setting are known, and the retest waits for contact time.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for starting dechlorination of chlorinated effluent.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: sodium bisulfite feed ahead of the outfall, plant licence requires a near zero total residual.

cards.label: Check the bisulfite storage level and feed pump readiness
Measure the total chlorine residual in the chlorinated effluent
Log the feed rate and the before and after residuals
Confirm the total residual is at the target near zero level
Collect a sample downstream of the mixing point
Start the bisulfite feed paced to the effluent flow

tasks.explanation: The incoming residual sizes the job, feed follows supply checks, and the downstream sample proves dechlorination before it is logged.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for taking a chlorine contact tank out of service.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: twin contact tanks, one remains in service for disinfection.

cards.label: Close the inlet gate to the tank being removed
Divert all effluent flow through the contact tank staying in service
Wash down the tank and secure the access points
Apply lockout to the tank mixer and feed equipment
Drain the tank contents back to the plant process
Stop the chlorine feed line serving that tank and isolate it

tasks.explanation: Disinfection capacity is preserved by diversion first, chemical feed is isolated before draining, and lockout precedes washdown.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for priming a hypochlorite metering pump that has lost prime.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: diaphragm metering pump drawing from a day tank.

cards.label: Open the priming bleed valve over a containment container
Run the pump until a steady, bubble free stream of chemical appears
Close the bleed valve
Open the discharge to the process and verify feed by tank drawdown
Record the priming and the drawdown check in the chemical log
Put on chemical gloves, goggles, and an apron and check the eyewash station
Check the day tank level and the suction line for blockages

tasks.explanation: Protective equipment comes first, the bleed stays open only until the stream is bubble free, and drawdown proves real feed after the discharge opens.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for starting a gravity thickener.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: circular gravity thickener receiving primary and waste sludge.

cards.label: Close the drain and open the supernatant return line
Inspect the drive, pickets, and overflow launder and clear debris
Check supernatant clarity and blanket depth at steady operation
Begin withdrawing thickened sludge from the bottom once a blanket forms
Start the thickener drive as the tank fills
Open the sludge feed and fill the thickener

tasks.explanation: Inspection and line up precede filling, bottom withdrawal waits for a blanket, and clarity plus blanket checks confirm steady operation.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for transferring thickened sludge to a digester.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: transfer pump between the gravity thickener and the anaerobic digester.

cards.label: Check the receiving digester level for available capacity
Sample the thickener underflow and confirm its solids concentration
Flush the transfer line and log the volume moved
Stop the pump at the target transfer volume
Start the transfer pump and monitor the digester level during the run
Line up the transfer valves from thickener to digester

tasks.explanation: Concentration and capacity are confirmed before lining up, the level is watched during transfer, and flushing plus logging close the job.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for starting an aerobic digester.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: empty aerobic digester with coarse bubble aeration.

cards.label: Fill the digester with waste sludge to the normal operating level
Inspect the tank, air piping, and diffusers and remove debris
Log the starting volume, oxygen, and pH
Allow stabilization time before any decanting is attempted
Measure dissolved oxygen and pH in the digester contents
Start the aeration blower and check for even air distribution

tasks.explanation: Filling precedes aeration, oxygen and pH establish the baseline, and decanting waits for stabilization.

tasks.prompt: Order the routine feeding steps for a heated anaerobic digester.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: daily scheduled feed of thickened sludge to a mesophilic digester.

cards.label: Review the feed sludge volume and concentration records for the day
Check the digester temperature and liquid level
Log the feed volume, temperature, and gas readings
Check gas production and the pressure relief system readings
Run the digester mixing or recirculation system during and after feeding
Feed the scheduled volume slowly through the feed line

tasks.explanation: Temperature and level set the safe feed amount, mixing follows feeding to distribute it, and gas readings confirm the digester response.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for decanting supernatant from an aerobic digester.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: aerobic digester ready for a decant cycle.

cards.label: Wait the full settling period without disturbing the tank
Stop the aeration blower and let the contents settle
Restart aeration and log the decanted volume
Close the decant valve as soon as solids begin to appear
Watch the decant stream for clarity as the level falls
Open the decant valve slowly to the supernatant return line

tasks.explanation: Settling must finish before the valve opens, clarity is watched throughout, the valve closes at the first solids, and aeration resumes last.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for starting a belt filter press dewatering run.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: belt press with polymer conditioning, cake discharge to a bin.

cards.label: Start the polymer make down and feed system and let the solution mature
Start the belt press drives and confirm tracking is centred
Start the sludge feed pump at a low rate
Adjust polymer dose by watching cake release and filtrate clarity
Confirm cake is discharging cleanly to the bin before leaving the unit
Inspect the belts, rollers, and safety guards and clear any old cake
Start the belt wash water system

tasks.explanation: Wash water and mature polymer must be ready before sludge arrives, drives are proven before feed, and dose is tuned on cake quality.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for shutting down a belt filter press at the end of a run.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: dewatering run complete, belts still loaded with cake.

cards.label: Stop the polymer feed
Stop the sludge feed pump
Hose down the area and log the cake produced and the run hours
Stop the wash water system
Stop the belt drives once cleaning is complete
Keep the belts running with wash water until the belts are clean

tasks.explanation: Feed and polymer stop first, the belts keep moving under wash until clean, and water stops only after the drives do.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for using a sludge drying bed cycle.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: outdoor sand drying bed, digested sludge ready for drying.

cards.label: Open the sludge inlet valve and admit digested sludge
Inspect the bed surface, sand layer, and underdrain outlet
Restore and level the sand surface for the next cycle
Remove the dried sludge from the bed surface
Allow drainage and drying until the sludge cracks and firms
Spread the sludge in an even layer across the bed

tasks.explanation: The bed is inspected before sludge is admitted, even spreading aids drying, removal waits for a firm cake, and bed restoration closes the cycle.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for loading liquid sludge into a tanker truck for hauling.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: load out from the liquid sludge storage tank to a licensed hauler.

cards.label: Inspect the tanker, hoses, and connections for leaks or damage
Confirm the sludge test records required for hauling are complete
Complete the hauling paperwork and record the volume shipped
Close the outlet valve and drain the hose before disconnecting
Load the tanker to its marked working level while monitoring the hose
Connect the loading hose and open the tank outlet valve

tasks.explanation: Paperwork readiness and equipment inspection precede loading, the hose is drained before disconnect to prevent spills, and records close the load.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for setting up a 24 hour composite sampler at the plant influent.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: refrigerated automatic sampler, flow paced sampling required.

cards.label: Place clean sample bottles in the sampler base
Check sampler power, suction tubing, and strainer condition
Confirm the first sample reached the bottle and log the setup
Prime the suction line and run a manual test sample
Set the program start time
Program the sampler for flow paced intervals and the correct sample volume

tasks.explanation: Hardware and bottles are ready before programming, priming proves the line, and a confirmed test sample validates the whole setup.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for measuring dissolved oxygen with a field meter.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: handheld DO meter with a membrane probe, measuring at the aeration basin.

cards.label: Rinse the probe with sample water
Check the meter calibration in water saturated air as the manual directs
Rinse the probe and store it in its moistened cap
Record the dissolved oxygen and the sample temperature
Wait for the reading to stabilize
Immerse the probe in the mixed liquor with gentle movement to avoid bubbles

tasks.explanation: Calibration precedes measurement, gentle movement prevents bubble error, the reading is recorded only when stable, and proper storage protects the probe.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for setting up a BOD5 test in the laboratory.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: standard five day BOD test on a wastewater sample.

cards.label: Prepare the dilution water with nutrients and confirm it is saturated with oxygen
Bring the sample to room temperature and check that its pH is in the method range
Place the bottles in the incubator at 20 C for five days
Measure and record the initial dissolved oxygen of each bottle
Fill the bottles with dilution water and stopper them with no air bubbles trapped
Measure the chosen sample volumes into the labelled BOD bottles

tasks.explanation: Sample condition and dilution water come before filling, initial oxygen must be measured before incubation, and incubation is the final step.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for completing a BOD5 test on day five.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: bottles completing five days of incubation at 20 C.

cards.label: Measure the final dissolved oxygen of each bottle promptly
Remove the bottles from the incubator after the full five days
Report the BOD result with any validity notes
Check the blank and seed results for test validity
Calculate the oxygen depletion using the dilution factor for each bottle
Record the final readings beside the initial readings

tasks.explanation: Final oxygen is measured promptly before it can change, depletion is calculated from paired readings, and validity is checked before reporting.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for a total suspended solids test.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: gravimetric TSS test using a pre weighed glass fibre filter.

cards.label: Filter the measured volume through the pre weighed filter
Mix the sample thoroughly and measure the test volume
Weigh the filter and calculate the suspended solids concentration
Cool the dried filter in a desiccator
Dry the filter in the oven at 103 to 105 C
Rinse the funnel and filter with distilled water to transfer all solids

tasks.explanation: All solids are captured and rinsed onto the filter before drying, desiccator cooling prevents moisture error, and weighing is last.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for running a 30 minute settleability test.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: mixed liquor settleability using a 1 L graduated cylinder.

cards.label: Mix the sample gently to resuspend the solids evenly
Collect a fresh mixed liquor sample at the basin outlet
Note the supernatant clarity and sludge appearance and report the result
Record the settled sludge volume at 30 minutes
Start the timer as soon as pouring finishes
Pour exactly 1 L into the graduated cylinder

tasks.explanation: A fresh, evenly mixed sample and an exact volume make the test valid, timing starts at pouring, and observation completes the record.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for determining the sludge volume index for a mixed liquor sample.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: SVI calculated from the settleability test and the solids test on the same sample.

cards.label: Obtain the mixed liquor suspended solids result for the same sample
Run the 30 minute settleability test on the sample
Report the SVI to process control with the settling observations
Compare the SVI with the plant target range
Calculate SVI by dividing the settled volume by the solids concentration with the standard unit conversion
Express the settled volume on a per litre basis

tasks.explanation: Both measurements must come from the same sample, the calculation follows them, and comparison plus reporting complete the determination.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for calibrating a bench pH meter and measuring a sample.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: two point calibration with pH 7 and pH 4 buffers.

cards.label: Rinse the electrode again
Immerse the electrode in pH 4 buffer and set the second calibration point
Rinse the electrode and immerse it in the sample
Record the sample pH and temperature once the reading is stable
Rinse the electrode and return it to its storage solution
Rinse the electrode with distilled water and blot it dry
Immerse the electrode in pH 7 buffer and set the calibration point

tasks.explanation: The neutral buffer anchors calibration before the acid buffer, rinsing between solutions prevents carryover, and storage solution protects the electrode last.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for collecting an effluent grab sample at the outfall sampling point.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: routine compliance grab sample, unpreserved container supplied by the lab.

cards.label: Collect the sample below the surface, facing the container opening into the flow
Check the sampling point for safe access and rinse the dipper with effluent
Complete the chain of custody form and log the collection
Place the sample in a cooler with ice
Label the container with the location, date, time, and sampler name
Fill the container fully and cap it tightly

tasks.explanation: Safe access and rinsing come first, labelling follows capping so the sample is identified, and cooling plus custody paperwork protect the result.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for measuring chlorine residual with the DPD method.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: colorimeter DPD test at the contact tank outlet.

cards.label: Fill the cell to the mark with sample
Rinse the sample cell with the water to be tested
Record the residual and rinse the cell clean
Read the cell in the colorimeter within the method time limit
Mix gently until the reagent dissolves and colour develops
Add the DPD reagent and cap the cell

tasks.explanation: Rinsing prevents carryover, reagent and mixing develop the colour, the reading must fall inside the method time window, and recording follows.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for preserving and shipping collected samples to the contract laboratory.

tasks.prompt: The grit classifier wash water runs constantly and the grit pile looks clean but very wet, with water ponding in the grit bin.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater plant case. Readings are from the stated shift unless a bench or paired check is noted. Archived plant records are available for follow up.

evidence.label: Classifier discharge grit drains poorly and a hand sample holds free water.
The classifier wash water valve was found open well past its set position and the flow meter reads three times the set wash rate.
Returning the valve to its set position on trial stopped the ponding within a shift.
Grit chamber capture upstream is normal and influent flow is unchanged.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The grit chamber is passing organic material that holds water in the pile
Excess classifier wash water from a valve left open past its setting is flooding the grit and causing the ponding
Groundwater is leaking into the grit bin from below
Rain is entering an uncovered bin and ponding on the grit

inference.explanation: Upstream capture is normal and the grit looks clean, which argues against organic carryover. No leak or rain pattern is recorded, and the trial closing of the valve stopped the ponding at once. The metered wash rate at three times setpoint directly supports excess wash water.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best distinguishes the supported explanation from the alternatives?

options.label: Classifier wash water meter record and valve position check sheet
Influent flow annual summary
Primary effluent turbidity log

nextClue.explanation: This check tests the supported explanation directly against the alternatives. The other choices do not isolate the cause shown by the evidence.

clueText.nc-a: The meter record shows the high wash rate starting the day the valve was last adjusted.
clueText.nc-b: Annual flow summaries cannot test classifier wash water.
clueText.nc-c: Primary effluent turbidity does not measure grit washing.

tasks.prompt: Chlorine gas detector alarms in the chlorine room, but staff find the cylinders closed and no visible leak at the valves.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater plant case. Readings are from the stated shift unless a bench or paired check is noted. Archived plant records are available for follow up.

evidence.label: The detector reads 3 ppm at a low point near the floor drain of the chlorine room.
A ammonia vapour check at a flexible connector joint produces a white cloud, showing a small chlorine leak at that joint.
Ventilation in the room is running and readings fall when the connector is isolated.
The detector passed its calibration gas check the same day.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The detector has failed and is alarming on clean air
Cleaning chemicals stored nearby are off gassing chlorine
The cylinders are leaking through their closed valves at a high rate
A small chlorine leak at the flexible connector is real and is collecting near the floor where the detector senses it

inference.explanation: The detector passes calibration and the ammonia check finds a leak at a specific joint, contradicting a false alarm and a storage source. Cylinder valves show no leak and readings fall when the connector is isolated, which locates the source at the connector.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best distinguishes the supported explanation from the alternatives?

options.label: Leak check record for the chlorine piping joints and detector calibration log
Effluent flow summary
Blower log

nextClue.explanation: This check tests the supported explanation directly against the alternatives. The other choices do not isolate the cause shown by the evidence.

clueText.nc-a: After the connector was replaced, detector readings stayed at zero with ventilation running.
clueText.nc-b: Flow summaries do not test chlorine leaks.
clueText.nc-c: Blower records cover aeration air.

tasks.prompt: Primary effluent suspended solids rose sharply on one of two identical parallel primary clarifiers while the other stayed normal.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater plant case. Readings are from the stated shift unless a bench or paired check is noted. Archived plant records are available for follow up.

evidence.label: Clarifier A effluent TSS is 210 mg/L and clarifier B effluent TSS is 95 mg/L at equal split flow.
Clarifier A sludge blanket is 1.6 m deep against 0.5 m in clarifier B.
Clarifier A sludge draw off line was found with its valve nearly closed, and opening it dropped the blanket within hours.
Influent TSS to both units is the same combined sample at 240 mg/L.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Clarifier A receives a stronger influent than clarifier B
Clarifier A drive has failed and the scraper is stopped
Restricted sludge draw off on clarifier A let its blanket rise until solids carried over the weir
A toxic discharge is killing settling in clarifier A only

inference.explanation: Both units share one influent sample, so a stronger feed to A is contradicted. A stopped drive would not be corrected by opening a draw off valve. The deep blanket plus the nearly closed valve and the recovery after opening it support restricted draw off.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best distinguishes the supported explanation from the alternatives?

options.label: Influent flow total for the month
Sludge draw off valve position record and blanket depth log for both clarifiers
Effluent chlorine log

nextClue.explanation: This check tests the supported explanation directly against the alternatives. The other choices do not isolate the cause shown by the evidence.

clueText.nc-a: Monthly flow totals cannot separate the two parallel units.
clueText.nc-b: The blanket log shows A rising for three days while its draw off valve sat nearly closed, and falling after it was opened.
clueText.nc-c: Chlorine records cover disinfection and do not test primary sludge draw off.

tasks.prompt: Primary sludge pumped to the digester is very thin and digester feed volume has doubled.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater plant case. Readings are from the stated shift unless a bench or paired check is noted. Archived plant records are available for follow up.

evidence.label: Primary sludge total solids read 1.2 percent against the usual 4 to 5 percent.
The sludge pump run time per day has doubled while blanket depth in the clarifier stays low at 0.2 m.
A check of the pumping schedule shows the pump timer was changed to much longer cycles last week.
Influent flow and TSS are normal, and clarifier effluent quality is unchanged.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The influent has become much weaker and the sludge is naturally thin
The digester is returning water to the clarifier and diluting the sludge
The sludge blanket has disappeared because settling has failed
Overpumping on the lengthened timer cycles is drawing water with the sludge and thinning the primary sludge

inference.explanation: Influent is normal and effluent quality is unchanged, so weak influent and failed settling are unsupported. The digester does not return water to the clarifier. Long pump cycles with a low blanket and thin sludge directly support overpumping.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best distinguishes the supported explanation from the alternatives?

options.label: Effluent ammonia log
Aeration blower log
Sludge pump timer settings and run time log against blanket depth records

nextClue.explanation: This check tests the supported explanation directly against the alternatives. The other choices do not isolate the cause shown by the evidence.

clueText.nc-a: Ammonia records do not test primary sludge pumping.
clueText.nc-b: Blower records cover aeration, not sludge draw off.
clueText.nc-c: Run times doubled the day the timer was changed, while blanket depth stayed low, matching thin sludge from that date.

tasks.prompt: Gas bubbles and rising sludge chunks appear on the surface of a primary clarifier on warm afternoons.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater plant case. Readings are from the stated shift unless a bench or paired check is noted. Archived plant records are available for follow up.

evidence.label: Sludge blanket depth is 1.4 m, the deepest recorded this season.
Primary sludge draw off from this unit was missed for two days during a pump repair.
Surface chunks test as old sludge and release gas when broken on a bench check.
Water temperature is 24 C and influent flow is at normal summer values.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Sludge held too long in the clarifier during the draw off outage went septic and is rising on gas
The scum baffle has failed and surface scum is escaping
Algae growth on the weirs is breaking off into the flow
The influent contains floating industrial plastic that looks like sludge

inference.explanation: The material tests as old sludge releasing gas, not scum, algae, or plastic. Warm water, the deepest blanket of the season, and two missed days of draw off during the pump repair fit septic rising sludge.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best distinguishes the supported explanation from the alternatives?

options.label: Sludge draw off outage record and blanket depth trend for the warm period
Screenings mass log
Effluent pH log

nextClue.explanation: This check tests the supported explanation directly against the alternatives. The other choices do not isolate the cause shown by the evidence.

clueText.nc-a: The trend shows the blanket climbing through the two day outage and gas lifting starting the following warm afternoon.
clueText.nc-b: Screenings records do not test clarifier sludge age.
clueText.nc-c: Effluent pH does not isolate septic rising sludge.

tasks.prompt: Primary clarifier effluent quality worsens only during the evening peak, then recovers overnight.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater plant case. Readings are from the stated shift unless a bench or paired check is noted. Archived plant records are available for follow up.

evidence.label: Evening peak flow reaches 1.9 times the daily average for about three hours.
Surface overflow rate at peak calculates above the design value posted for the unit, and within it the rest of the day.
Sludge blanket stays near 0.4 m through the peak and sludge draw off is normal.
A second identical clarifier is out of service for drive repair, so all flow passes through one unit.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The evening influent is much stronger in solids than the morning influent
With one clarifier out of service, the evening peak overloads the remaining unit hydraulically and solids wash out until flow falls
The sludge blanket is rising at night and sloughing in the evening
The scraper drive slows down every evening on a timer fault

inference.explanation: Blanket depth stays normal and draw off is normal, which argues against blanket sloughing. No drive fault is recorded, and the worsening tracks flow timing. Peak overflow rate above design with half the clarifier capacity out of service supports hydraulic overload.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best distinguishes the supported explanation from the alternatives?

options.label: Digester temperature log
Hourly flow record and the clarifier in service log for the affected evenings
Chlorine day tank level log

nextClue.explanation: This check tests the supported explanation directly against the alternatives. The other choices do not isolate the cause shown by the evidence.

clueText.nc-a: Digester temperature does not test clarifier hydraulics.
clueText.nc-b: The records show effluent quality falling only in the hours when peak flow passed through the single unit in service.
clueText.nc-c: Chlorine tank levels do not explain primary washout timing.

tasks.prompt: Black, odorous sludge and low pH are found in a primary clarifier that receives sewage after long upstream holding.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater plant case. Readings are from the stated shift unless a bench or paired check is noted. Archived plant records are available for follow up.

evidence.label: Incoming sewage pH is 6.4 and it carries a septic odour at the inlet.
The upstream force main and wet well system holds sewage about 8 hours before it reaches the plant.
Primary sludge volatile acids are elevated on a bench test and the sludge is black.
Clarifier mechanics, blanket depth, and draw off are all normal on inspection.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The clarifier scraper has failed and sludge is rotting in place
A cleaning chemical spill at the plant lowered the pH
Sewage arriving already septic from long upstream holding is driving the black odorous sludge and low pH in the clarifier
The sludge pump is leaking digester supernatant into the clarifier

inference.explanation: Mechanics and draw off are normal, so in place rotting from a failed scraper is unsupported. No spill is recorded and no supernatant line connects to the clarifier. Septic inlet conditions with long upstream holding and elevated volatile acids support sewage that arrives septic.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best distinguishes the supported explanation from the alternatives?

options.label: Effluent turbidity log
Blower air flow log
Upstream holding time record and inlet pH and odour log for the affected days

nextClue.explanation: This check tests the supported explanation directly against the alternatives. The other choices do not isolate the cause shown by the evidence.

clueText.nc-a: Effluent turbidity does not test influent septicity.
clueText.nc-b: Blower records cover the aeration process, not influent condition.
clueText.nc-c: Inlet pH was lowest and odour strongest after the longest upstream holding periods.

tasks.prompt: Scum is escaping over the primary clarifier effluent weir and showing up in the aeration tank.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater plant case. Readings are from the stated shift unless a bench or paired check is noted. Archived plant records are available for follow up.

evidence.label: The scum baffle in front of the weir is found hanging loose with a gap at one end on inspection.
Scum layer thickness on the surface is normal and the scum skimmer is removing scum to the pit as usual.
Clarifier effluent TSS is only slightly above normal, so the escaping material is surface scum, not settled solids.
Flow and blanket depth are both normal.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The skimmer has failed and scum has built up until it overflows
High flow is pushing the whole surface over the weir
Grease in the influent has suddenly doubled and overwhelms the unit
The loose scum baffle with a gap is letting surface scum pass under it to the effluent weir

inference.explanation: Skimmer operation and scum thickness are normal, so build up from skimmer failure is contradicted. Flow is normal and TSS is near normal, which argues against hydraulic push over or a grease surge. The baffle gap found on inspection directly explains scum at the weir.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best distinguishes the supported explanation from the alternatives?

options.label: Scum baffle inspection record and skimmer operation log for the week
Influent BOD log
Waste sludge log

nextClue.explanation: This check tests the supported explanation directly against the alternatives. The other choices do not isolate the cause shown by the evidence.

clueText.nc-a: The inspection record notes the baffle gap on the same side where scum was seen leaving.
clueText.nc-b: BOD records do not test a baffle gap.
clueText.nc-c: Waste sludge records belong to the secondary process.

tasks.prompt: Primary treatment removal efficiency dropped across the whole plant over two weeks.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater plant case. Readings are from the stated shift unless a bench or paired check is noted. Archived plant records are available for follow up.

evidence.label: TSS removal fell from 62 percent to 41 percent while influent TSS stayed near 230 mg/L.
Both clarifiers show the drop equally and both are mechanically sound on inspection.
A settling aid trial that was improving removal was stopped two weeks ago when the trial chemical ran out.
Flows are normal and blanket depths and draw off are normal on both units.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Stopping the settling aid trial two weeks ago matches the plant wide drop in primary removal
Both clarifier drives are failing at the same time
The influent became harder to settle because its strength doubled
The lab began under reading effluent TSS two weeks ago

inference.explanation: Both drives inspect sound and influent strength is unchanged, so those options are unsupported. A lab under reading of effluent TSS would raise, not lower, reported removal. The timing of the stopped trial matching a drop shared by both units supports the settling aid explanation.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best distinguishes the supported explanation from the alternatives?

options.label: Chlorine residual log
Trial chemical delivery and dosing log against the removal efficiency trend
Digester gas log

nextClue.explanation: This check tests the supported explanation directly against the alternatives. The other choices do not isolate the cause shown by the evidence.

clueText.nc-a: Chlorine records do not test primary settling.
clueText.nc-b: Removal held near 62 percent through the trial and fell within days of the last dosing day.
clueText.nc-c: Digester gas does not measure clarifier removal.

tasks.prompt: Short circuiting is suspected in a circular primary clarifier because dye appears at the outlet far too quickly.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater plant case. Readings are from the stated shift unless a bench or paired check is noted. Archived plant records are available for follow up.

evidence.label: A dye test shows first colour at the effluent weir in 18 minutes against a theoretical detention of 2.1 hours.
The inlet baffle ring is found partly detached, leaving a direct path from inlet to one side.
Effluent TSS is worst on the same side where dye arrived first.
Flow during the test was at the normal average rate and blanket depth was normal.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The clarifier is far too small for the plant flow at all times
The partly detached inlet baffle is letting flow short circuit from inlet to outlet on one side
Density currents from cold influent alone explain the dye result
The dye test itself was done at excessive flow and is invalid

inference.explanation: The test ran at normal flow, so an invalid high flow test is contradicted. A unit too small at all times would not produce a one sided pattern tied to a baffle gap, and no cold influent was recorded. The detached baffle, one sided dye arrival, and one sided poor effluent support short circuiting at the baffle.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best distinguishes the supported explanation from the alternatives?

options.label: Screenings log
Effluent ammonia log
Dye test record and inlet baffle inspection report for the unit

nextClue.explanation: This check tests the supported explanation directly against the alternatives. The other choices do not isolate the cause shown by the evidence.

clueText.nc-a: Screenings records do not test clarifier flow paths.
clueText.nc-b: Ammonia records do not trace detention in the clarifier.
clueText.nc-c: The dye record shows first arrival on the side of the baffle gap, matching the poor effluent side.

tasks.prompt: Primary sludge blanket is normal but the clarifier effluent carries fine particles that do not settle.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater plant case. Readings are from the stated shift unless a bench or paired check is noted. Archived plant records are available for follow up.

evidence.label: A bench settling test on influent shows fine dispersed particles that stay suspended after 2 hours.
The same fine material passes both primary clarifiers equally.
A new metal finishing discharge began upstream last week, and its sample shows a milky dispersed character.
Clarifier surface overflow rate and blanket control are within normal values.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Both clarifiers are hydraulically overloaded at normal flows
The sludge scrapers are stirring settled solids back into the effluent
A dispersed industrial discharge upstream is bringing non settleable fine particles that the primary clarifiers cannot remove by gravity
The lab settling test was done with a broken cylinder and is invalid

inference.explanation: Overflow rate is normal, so overload is unsupported, and scraper stirring would raise settled solids rather than pass a milky influent unchanged. The bench test matches the upstream sample character and the timing of the new discharge, supporting non settleable dispersed solids in the influent.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best distinguishes the supported explanation from the alternatives?

options.label: Upstream discharge sample results and the influent bench settling record
Blower run log
Chlorine log

nextClue.explanation: This check tests the supported explanation directly against the alternatives. The other choices do not isolate the cause shown by the evidence.

clueText.nc-a: The upstream sample and the plant influent show the same dispersed character in settling tests done the same week.
clueText.nc-b: Blower records do not test influent settleability.
clueText.nc-c: Chlorine records do not explain primary fine particles.
